titulo: Explainer: South Korea’s Constitutional Court to Consider Presidents’ Ouster

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: The impeachment late last month of South Korea’s acting President Han Duck-soo has deepened political division in the country. He had replaced President Yoon Suk Yeol, who was impeached earlier in December.

Two impeachments suspending the country’s top two officials in a short period of time has never happened before in South Korea. Now, the deputy prime minister and finance minister, Choi Sang-mok, is the new temporary leader.

When he took power, Choi quickly ordered the military to increase readiness in the event of an act of aggression by North Korea. Diplomats communicated with important partners including the United States and Japan.
Duyeon Kim is an expert with the Center for a New American Security in Washington, D.C. Kim said: “(Han’s) impeachment now creates an opportunity for external threats.”
Before Yoon declared martial law on December 3, Han Duck-soo was the prime minister and the second highest official in South Korea. Lawmakers impeached Yoon on December 14 over his martial law order.

Han tried to ease the concerns of South Korea’s major diplomatic partners and to calm its financial markets. However, he became involved in a political dispute with the opposition Democratic Party, or DP.

DP lawmakers demanded that Han immediately appoint three justices to seats on the Constitutional Court to rule on Yoon’s impeachment. The court normally has nine justices. Currently three seats remain open. Han refused to fill the open seats. He said he would not appoint justices without the approval of both the DP and the governing People Power Party, or PPP.

Choi Jin is director of the Institute of Presidential Leadership based in Seoul. He said Han lacked a good reason not to appoint the justices. But Choi said the DP should not have moved to impeach Han so quickly.

Han’s impeachment came as South Korean officials told international partners that the situation was returning to normal. Officials in Japan, Europe and the United States had been surprised by Yoon’s declaration of martial law.

Duyeon Kim said: “South Korea is now in a far more serious crisis of leadership and governance,” adding that, “Han had the experience and credentials to deal with both security and financial crises….”

The governing party argues that Han’s impeachment is “invalid” because it is based on a simple majority of the 300-member National Assembly. The PPP says a two-thirds majority is necessary. It has brought a case before the Constitutional Court to consider the impeachment vote of Yoon.

The Constitutional Court has 180 days to decide on the legality of both impeachments. Han called his impeachment “regrettable,” but said he respects the assembly’s decision. If Yoon is ousted, then a national election must take place within 60 days.
Yoon faces several separate investigations into possible wrongdoing linked to his martial law declaration. DP leader Lee Jae-myung is favored to win a possible presidential election.

However, Lee faces legal cases as well. He was found guilty of election law violations in November. He is appealing the ruling. If Lee becomes president, his trials would be suspended because South Korean law does not permit a sitting president to face legal action for most crimes.

titulo_es: Explainer: South Korea’s Constitutional Court to rule on the impeachment of the presidents
resumen_es: Explains the South Korean political crisis after the impeachment by parliament of President Yoon, who declared martial law, and of his acting replacement Han, and the role of the Constitutional Court, which must rule on both.
nivel_motivo: The political and institutional vocabulary (impeachment, justices, martial law, credentials) raises the calculated level, but the sentences are clear and the adapted text includes a glossary, so it fits B2.

ideas_clave.idea: For the first time, South Korea's two highest officials have been impeached in quick succession, and the finance minister, Choi Sang-mok, has become interim leader.
Choi put the armed forces on alert against North Korea and reassured allies, while experts warn that the turmoil invites external threats.
Yoon was impeached over his declaration of martial law on 3 December; his prime minister Han then took over and tried to reassure partners and markets, but clashed with the opposition.
The dispute centred on Han's refusal to fill three vacant seats on the Constitutional Court without the agreement of both main parties, although analysts criticised both sides.
Han's removal came just as officials were telling foreign partners that the situation was stabilising, deepening a crisis of leadership.
The ruling party disputes the validity of Han's impeachment, and the Court has 180 days to rule on both cases; if Yoon is removed, an election must follow within 60 days.
Yoon is under investigation, while opposition leader Lee Jae-myung, the favourite in any election, has his own convictions on appeal, which would be suspended if he became president.

resumen_modelo: The text explains the unprecedented political crisis in South Korea, where the two highest officials were impeached within a few weeks. President Yoon Suk Yeol was removed by parliament after declaring martial law in December, and his successor, Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, was impeached soon afterwards. Han had tried to reassure allies and markets, but he clashed with the opposition Democratic Party by refusing to fill three vacant seats on the Constitutional Court without cross-party agreement. As a result, the finance minister, Choi Sang-mok, is now interim leader and has placed the military on alert. Moreover, the governing party claims that Han's impeachment is invalid, arguing that a two-thirds majority was required. The Constitutional Court now has 180 days to rule on both cases. Finally, should Yoon be removed, an election would take place within 60 days, and opposition leader Lee Jae-myung, himself facing legal cases, would be the favourite.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: South Korea had already experienced two impeachments of its top officials in a short period before.
preguntas.cita: Two impeachments suspending the country’s top two officials in a short period of time has never happened before in South Korea.
preguntas.explicacion: The text stresses that it is the first time something like this has happened in South Korea.

preguntas.pregunta: Who is the new temporary leader of South Korea?
preguntas.cita: Now, the deputy prime minister and finance minister, Choi Sang-mok, is the new temporary leader.
preguntas.explicacion: Choi, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is the new acting leader. Han and Yoon have been impeached by parliament and Lee is the leader of the opposition.

preguntas.pregunta: What were Choi's first actions after taking power, and why?
respuestas: He ordered the armed forces to be more prepared in case North Korea attacked, and diplomats contacted key partners such as the United States and Japan, in order to prevent the political crisis from creating security risks.
preguntas.cita: Choi quickly ordered the military to increase readiness in the event of an act of aggression by North Korea.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must cover the military alert order and the diplomatic contacts, and link them to the fear of external threats mentioned in the text.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 4 an expression that means “a system in which the army takes control and civil rights are suspended”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression for military rule that temporarily replaces normal civilian law.
preguntas.cita: Before Yoon declared martial law on December 3
preguntas.explicacion: “Martial law” (es: ley marcial); in the Spanish context it would be associated with the “estado de sitio” (state of siege).

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Lawmakers impeached Yoon because of his martial law order.
preguntas.cita: Lawmakers impeached Yoon on December 14 over his martial law order.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so explicitly: he was impeached by parliament on 14 December because of his martial law order.

preguntas.pregunta: Why did Han refuse to appoint three new justices to the Constitutional Court?
opciones: Because the court already had nine justices
Because he wanted the approval of both the DP and the PPP
Because Yoon had ordered him not to
Because the Court had already ruled on Yoon's case
respuestas: Because he wanted the approval of both the DP and the PPP
preguntas.cita: He said he would not appoint justices without the approval of both the DP and the governing People Power Party
preguntas.explicacion: Han demanded the agreement of both parties. The court normally has nine justices, but three seats are vacant; the points about Yoon and a previous ruling do not appear in the text.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 6 a word for the judges of a high court.
preguntas.pregunta: Find the word used for the judges of the Constitutional Court.
preguntas.cita: DP lawmakers demanded that Han immediately appoint three justices to seats on the Constitutional Court
preguntas.explicacion: “Justices” are the judges of a high court. False friend: it does not mean “justicias” in an abstract sense.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: According to Choi Jin, the DP was right to impeach Han so quickly.
preguntas.cita: But Choi said the DP should not have moved to impeach Han so quickly.
preguntas.explicacion: Choi Jin criticises both sides: Han had no reason not to appoint the justices, but the DP should not have impeached him so quickly.

preguntas.pregunta: How does Duyeon Kim describe Han?
opciones: As responsible for the martial law declaration
As having the experience and credentials to manage security and financial crises
As a weak leader who lacked international contacts
As the favourite to win the next election
respuestas: As having the experience and credentials to manage security and financial crises
preguntas.cita: Han had the experience and credentials to deal with both security and financial crises
preguntas.explicacion: Kim values Han’s experience. Martial law was declared by Yoon, and the favourite in an election is Lee Jae-myung.

preguntas.pregunta: On what grounds does the governing party consider Han's impeachment invalid?
respuestas: It argues that the vote only obtained a simple majority of the 300-member National Assembly, whereas in its view a two-thirds majority was required.
preguntas.cita: The PPP says a two-thirds majority is necessary.
preguntas.explicacion: The PPP’s argument is procedural: according to the party, the impeachment required a two-thirds majority, not a simple one.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: If Yoon is removed from office, a presidential election must be held within 60 days.
preguntas.cita: If Yoon is ousted, then a national election must take place within 60 days.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so explicitly; the court in turn has 180 days to decide.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Yoon has been arrested and is currently in prison.
preguntas.explicacion: The text only says that Yoon faces several investigations; it does not mention any arrest or imprisonment.

preguntas.pregunta: What would happen to Lee Jae-myung's trials if he became president?
opciones: They would be transferred to the Constitutional Court
preguntas.cita: If Lee becomes president, his trials would be suspended
preguntas.explicacion: South Korean law prevents a sitting president from being prosecuted for most crimes, so the trials would be suspended, not cancelled or moved.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 13 a word that means “currently holding office”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'currently holding office'.
preguntas.cita: South Korean law does not permit a sitting president to face legal action for most crimes
preguntas.explicacion: A “sitting president” is the president currently in office; “incumbent” is also used.
